learning: Iteration 0 has no telemetry. Next iteration, use rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation to tune kp and kd first. Raise base_speed only if completion_time is well under 3 s with no line losses.
notes: Baseline Builder geometry with a proportional-derivative controller. Weights follow sensor x-position so the signal sign matches the steering convention. Expected to be confirmed or revised by the first race.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so the controller is a conservative, physics-based starting point. The geometry is the Builder's baseline, kept unchanged. Five sensors sit at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, so I set sensor_weights proportional to each sensor's sideways position: [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. This makes a positive signal (line to the robot's left) steer left, as the contract requires. Because the signal is a reading-weighted average, its magnitude stays within about ±2. kp = 1.0 gives a turn of up to about ±2, which is 700 PWM counts of differential at full deflection. That is firm enough to hold the line through moderate bends without saturating. kd = 0.2 damps oscillation at speed. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on a curved course. base_speed = 1.5 gives 75 percent PWM, which should give an average speed near the 1.5 m/s needed to finish in under 3 s. line_loss = 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it last saw the tape, which suits a single curved line. I expect completion with modest rms_error, but this is unverified until the race returns data.
